notes.claim: A diode is an electrical component acting as a one-way valve for current.
Silicon diodes have a forward voltage of approximately 0.7 volts.
A diode has a maximum reverse-bias voltage it can withstand without breaking down, called the peak inverse voltage.
A meter on its diode range gives a forward reading typically below 0.7 volts for silicon, because the meter supplies only a trivial current.
Exceeding a normal diode’s PIV usually destroys the diode.
Use a meter’s diode check function for semiconductor devices and its resistance function for anything else.
On its resistance function a meter may output too low a test voltage to forward-bias a PN junction.
